title: Jean de Langeac, bishop of Avranches, Venice, to Montmorency, 14 Jan 1529, BnF fr. 3083 no. 8 ff. 20-21 (catalogue item 6, Avranches' cipher 1)

steps.what: Matched the four items against Tomokiyo's francis.htm and GL.htm: four letters, four different keys, all tabulated by Lasry in 2023; no plaintext on either site.
Located the correct Gallica arks (fr. 3091 is btv1b9060253s, not the catalogue's) and fetched full-resolution canvases.
Applied Lasry's 'Avranches' cipher 1' table to the 11 cipher lines of f. 21r by eye from line strips; the block opens MONSEIGNEVR DE SAINCT POL.
Read the cipher in full apart from a group of 3-4 signs before 'sans' and 2 signs before VNG; refined the table (ɓ = P/I, long-tailed 9 = A/V, 8∞ = LE, macron = n).
Dated to 14 Jan 1529 by Saint-Pol's command in Lombardy and the clear news of Aquila retaken in the Abruzzi campaign of winter 1528-29.

Correction from George Lasry: he decoded all four texts in 2023 when reconstructing the keys, but the decipherments were never published. Prior-solution record updated: a reading existed, unpublished, learned of after the reading and not used (only his keys were).

Split the combined catalogue item 6 entry under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): four letters in four keys. gramont1529 keeps fr. 3091 no. 23 (Gramont's cipher 1529); langeac1529 takes fr. 3083 no. 8 (Avranches' cipher 1); gramont1530 takes fr. 3071 no. 7 (Gramont's cipher 1530); the Mâcon letter fr. 3071 no. 4 moved to rome1536 with the other letters in Mascon's cipher. This entry is fr3083_no8_langeac.md, moved from targets/gramont1529/.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Lasry's 2023 table 'Avranches' cipher 1' for this letter (cryptiana GL.htm); no new cryptanalysis.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted 14 Oct 2026 from fr3083_no8_langeac.md: 442 plaintext letters deciphered in the cipher block against about 6 unread signs (a group of 3-4 and one of 2). Plaintext letters, not cipher signs: no alias file was kept for the 11 lines.
outcome.notes: Read in full apart from two short groups (about 6 signs) in lines 7 and 9.
